newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SOCCER-UNITED SUFFER INJURY BLOW AHEAD OF CRUCIAL CUP TIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNITED SUFFER INJURY BLOW AHEAD OF CRUCIAL CUP TIE.

text.p: Manchester United's bid to remain in the hunt for European silverware has suffered a blow on the eve of their do-or-die Champions' League clash with Rapid Vienna on Wednesday.

The English champions, who require at least a draw to stay in the running for a quarter-final berth, left for Vienna on Tuesday minus striker Paul Scholes who was ruled out by a thigh injury and illness. His absence looks certain to give Ole Gunnar Solskjaer a place in the starting line-up.

"He's had the thigh problem for four or five weeks and been able to play with it," said assistant manager Brian Kidd. "But just recently it has got a little worse and what he needs now is rest and treatment."
Apart from Phil Neville and Andy Cole -- United's two long-term injuries -- manager Alex Ferguson's team are otherwise at full strength for the final Group C game.
United welcome back England international Gary Pallister, who has suffered from a recurring back injury, at the heart of a defence which leaked goals during his absence.

The English club will need a victory if Turkey's Fenerbahce steal a result against European champions Juventus in Turin, but Rapid will only be playing for pride as they have already failed to qualify for the next round.
"We are going there to win," said Solskjaer. "We must win as I can see Juventus and Fenerbahce drawing. But if we win we have done our job.
"I think we were unlucky not to get a draw against Juventus and Fenerbahce at Old Trafford, but that is in the past. We must do the job in Vienna now."
United slumped to their second consecutive home defeat in the competition last month, losing 1-0 to Juventus after crashing three weeks earlier to Fenerbahce.
Ferguson's side have also slipped off the pace in the English premier league and lie in fifth place, five points adrift of leaders Arsenal.
Solskjaer scored once in United's 2-0 victory over Rapid at Old Trafford in September, earning comparisons with Jean-Pierre Papin from partner Eric Cantona.
"Rapid are a good side, but I think we are better," the Norwegian forward said. "Every match in Europe away from home is difficult.

"They have something to prove to their supporters and will go into the match with one thing in mind -- to win. It will be the biggest match of my career so far, if I play. So I am looking forward to the chance."
The Austrian first division leaders boast an unbeaten home run stretching back 15 ties, which formed the basis of their run to last season's European Cup Winners' Cup final.
Even reigning champions Juventus had to settle for a 1-1 draw, just a fortnight before they hammered Rapid 5-0 in the return game at the Delle Alpi.
Coach Ernst Dokupil scrapped the club's usual Sunday training before a Champions' League match and did not bother to send a "spy" to Manchester's 3-1 victory over premier league rival Leicester.

Rapid manager Werner Kuhn was also not too upset Manchester had ignored all his requests for a video of the English club's latest matches. Instead, he said players would study videos from their previous games against Juventus.
Rapid players, who started their winter holiday break from the Austrian league two weeks ago, took time off from practice last week to record and promote a new Christmas single.
Suspended Polish defender Andrzej Lesiak is the only regular player who will be missing from Rapid's squad.
Likely teams:
Rapid Vienna: Michael Konsel, Peter Guggi, Trifon Ivanov, Peter Schoettel, Didi Kuehbauer, Christian Prosenik, Krzysztof Ratajczyk, Thomas Zingler, Peter Stoeger, Andreas Heraf, Rene Wagner.
Manchester United: Peter Schmeichel, Gary Neville, Dennis Irwin, David May, Gary Pallister, Roy Keane, Eric Cantona, Nicky Butt, David Beckham, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Ryan Giggs.
